source_text: ut Deus hominum, sicut universi conditor, et iustus et verax ac pius, idem donorum suorum in homines cumulator probetur; quia una est - ut fateris - optima causa studiorum bonorum, ut honoretur Deus difficilis paucisque conveniens eruditis sanctarum cognitio Litterarum
pass_a_gloss: So-that/as God of-human-beings, as universi founder, and just and verax and godly, the-same donorum suorum in human-beings cumulator probetur; because together is - so-that/as fateris - optima case/cause studiorum bonorum, so-that/as with-honor God hard paucisque conveniens eruditis sanctarum cognitio Litterarum.

lemmas.lexica: LS conditor; Blaise God as maker from nothing

pass_b_english: Knowledge of the holy writings is difficult and suited to few learned people.
The aim is to establish that God, the creator of humanity and of the universe, is just, truthful, and good, and that he continually adds to his gifts to human beings.
There is one best reason for good studies: that God should be honored.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
